title: 3 · Loops (Deep Dive)
learn:
The story: the washing machine

A washing machine repeats spin cycles until a condition says stop. Loops are the same idea: repeat code while a condition holds. Every loop has a loop control variable with three life stages: initialised before, tested in the condition, updated inside. Skip the update and the condition never becomes false: an infinite loop.

Choosing the right loop

while: checks first, may run zero times; use when you do not know how many repeats. do-while: checks after, runs at least once (menus, “enter a valid age”), and ends with a semicolon. for: initialise; condition; update in one line, ideal when the count is known. Enhanced for (for-each): visits every element of an array or list with no index, but you cannot change the array safely or know the position.

Patterns you must be able to write

Accumulator: total += x. Counter: count++ when a condition holds. Max/min: start with the first element, replace when you find a bigger or smaller one. Sentinel loop: keep reading until the user types a stop value like -1. Nested loops: the inner loop runs completely for every step of the outer one, so 3 outer by 4 inner runs the body 12 times (stars triangles, multiplication tables, 2D arrays).

break and continue

break exits the loop immediately. continue skips the rest of this round and moves to the next.

Off-by-one errors

The most common loop bug. i <= 5 runs 5 times from 1 but i <= length on an array runs one step too far and throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Use i < arr.length.

Tracing

Exam questions give you code and ask the output. Draw a table with a column per variable and a row per iteration. Never trust your eyes.
